desc:
Decide whether the string s is a valid number literal. A valid literal has a decimal part optionally followed by an exponent, with nothing else around it.

  • The decimal part is an optional sign (+ or -) followed by one of: digits only (12); digits, a dot and optional digits (12., 12.5); or a dot followed by at least one digit (.5).
  • The exponent is the letter e or E, an optional sign, and at least one digit (e10, E-3, e+7). It is allowed only after a decimal part.

Valid: 2, 0089, -0.1, +3.14, 4., -.9, 2e10, -90E3, 3e+7, 53.5e93. Invalid: abc, 1a, 1e, e3, 99e2.5, --6, -+3, 95a54e53, ., +., .e1.
constraints: s contains letters, digits and the characters + - .; it has no spaces
hints: Write the grammar down as a sequence of optional and mandatory parts: sign, integer digits, dot, fraction digits, exponent marker, exponent sign, exponent digits.
Scan left to right with an index. Count how many digits you saw before and after the dot: the decimal part is valid only if at least one of the two counts is positive.
Handle the exponent last: it needs an e or E, an optional sign, and then at least one digit. After a successful scan the index has to be exactly at the end of the string.
editorial: A scanner that follows the grammar directly is the cleanest solution. Skip an optional sign. Count the digits of the integer part. If a dot follows, consume it and count the digits of the fractional part. The decimal part is acceptable only if the two counts add up to more than zero; this accepts 4. and .5 but rejects a lone ..

Next, if the current character is e or E, consume it, an optional sign, and the exponent digits, requiring at least one digit. If any step fails, return false. The literal is valid when the scan finished exactly at the end of the string, because leftovers such as the extra dot in 99e2.5 must make it invalid.

The same logic can be written as a finite automaton with states such as start, after sign, integer digits, after dot, fraction digits, after e, exponent sign, exponent digits. The scanner is linear time and constant space.
